hypotheses.content: Several molecules occupy a condition-sensitive long-retention tail in which V1, V2, and interval width can change substantially with PE/EA and loading conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The Row-distribution includes rare late and broad elutions; labels in this tail can calibrate both endpoints and reduce extrapolation error where absolute errors are likely large.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected weaker and stronger conditions produce smooth endpoint shifts, or are some scaffolds intrinsically nonmonotonic on silica?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, loading-solvent volume, and loading solvent can materially alter observed endpoint position and interval width, and these effects are partly confounded with mobile-phase strength in the seed.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor must learn whether density-times-volume features shift retention independently of PE/EA; paired measurements can improve its structure-condition-loading interaction representation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and mobile phase, how much do sample volume and loading-solvent volume move V1, V2, and width?

hypotheses.content: Candidates with large quantile widths and high CW distance sample sparse model regions where new labels should have disproportionate value for overall calibration.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These rows probe regions with limited local support and can improve uncertainty calibration and feature-space interpolation across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After retraining, do labels from high-width or high-CW rows reduce errors in nearby unlabeled chemical-condition neighborhoods?

hypotheses.content: Low-similarity molecule-novel rows are needed to test transfer of retention relationships across aromaticity, halogenation, heteroatoms, and hydrogen-bonding environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The catalog contains structure gaps; a small set of chemically distinct labels can improve generalization beyond dense scaffold families without spending the batch on arbitrary diversity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can QGeoGNN transfer silica-retention trends from labeled scaffolds to these low-similarity structures?

hypotheses.content: Same-molecule condition-response curves are more informative than isolated points when measured rows already show large shifts across PE/EA or loading conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local curves teach the retrained model monotonicity, interaction terms, and endpoint-width changes while connecting labels to structurally similar rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do intermediate conditions interpolate the measured endpoint shifts well enough to improve predictions at unmeasured PE/EA ratios?

batch_rationale: The batch combines five complementary sources of learning value. High-width and high-CW rows target sparse regions and late-elution tails that can dominate absolute V1/V2 error. Several same-molecule sets deliberately form response curves: m161, m92, m90, m11, m39, and m125. These curves test mobile-phase response and distinguish smooth interpolation from abrupt or scaffold-specific behavior. m20, m99, and m104 add loading and loading-solvent comparisons where the seed shows substantial endpoint variation. The molecule-novel m120, m157, m152, m155, m135, and m189 rows provide controlled chemical-space exploration with low similarity to labeled structures. Together, the batch repairs likely tail and interaction gaps while preserving coverage of ordinary and novel rows, which should improve generalization across the full Row-distribution after retraining.
